paragraphs.text: {See Trapp on "Exo 33:7"}
paragraphs.anchor: Ver. l. Which thou hast brought.

paragraphs.text: A created angel to conduct thee. But Moses would none of that; he would not be so put off. {Exo 34:9} Low things satisfy not a high spirit.
sc., By those visible signs of my gracious presence as heretofore.
As good cause they had: for "woe be unto thee when I depart from thee." {Hos 9:12}

God’s threatenings are cordial, but conditional. Minatur Deus ut non puniat. "Fury is not in me." {Isa 27:4} He punisheth not "till there be no other remedy," {2Ch 36:16} as the bee stings not till provoked.
As in a day of restraint.
In token of God’s deep displeasure and departure from them.
To see what success, what acceptance: as David looked up after his prayer to see how it sped. {Psa 5:3}
Out of the cloudy pillar: which was a sign of favour. {Psa 99:7} The Turks honour Moses, and call him the talker with God.
paragraphs.anchor: And the Lord talked with Moses.

paragraphs.text: Though obnoxious, they would not despair of mercy. See 1Sa 12:20-22.
Friendly and familiarly, as Num 12:8. And perhaps in human shape, as he spake with Abraham his friend. Gen 18:16-33

See, saith one, {a} how Moses here encroacheth upon God. God had done much for him, he must have more. {Exo 33:13} "Show me now thy way," &c. This God grants him. {Exo 33:14} This serves not the turn; he must have more yet. {Exo 33:16} Well, he hath it. {Exo 33:17} Is he satisfied? No, he must yet have more. {Exo 33:18} "I beseech thee show me thy glory." It is done. {Exo 33:19} Is he satisfied yet? No. {Exo 34:9} God must pardon the sin of his people too; and take them and him for his inheritance: this fruit of his favour he must needs be entreated to add to the rest.
{a} Mr Bur. [?Burroughs.]

Moses knew more of God than any man; he was but newly come down from the mount, and at the tabernacle door God spake with Moses "face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend." {Exo 33:11} The more a man knows of God, the more desirous he is to know him.
Full content of mind, in the sense of my presence and light of my countenance.
What is it to have the air without light? What was all Mordecai’s honour to him when the king frowned upon him?
paragraphs.anchor: If thy presence go not with me.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Marvellously separated. The separation of the saints is a wonderful separation. See Deu 4:7; also Isa 20:6, where Judea is for this cause called an "isle."
As princes do their favourites, who easily forget others, as Saul did David. {1Sa 17:55}
None ever knew God’s glory; our cockle shell can never comprehend this sea: yet it may be apprehended that it is incomprehensible.
My glorious goodness. Thus Moses may have what he will of God. "The king is not he that can do anything against you," said Zedekiah to his courtiers. {Jer 38:5}
paragraphs.anchor: I will make all my goodness.

paragraphs.text: Otherwise than in his words and works. {Rom 1:20} As we cannot see the sun in rota, in the circle, but in the beams. Some have seen Mercabah velo harocheb, as the Hebrews speak, {a} the chariot in which God rode, but not the rider in it: they saw some created image, or glory, whereby he testified his more immediate presence, but not himself.
paragraphs.anchor: Thou canst not see my face.

paragraphs.text: But be oppressed and swallowed up with majesty: as the sight of the eye is dazzled with the sun; or a crystal glass broken with the fire.
paragraphs.anchor: No man shall see me, and live.

paragraphs.text: {a} Rab. Maimon.
